Novhorod-Siverskyy Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Novhorod-Siverskyy's Jewish settlement dates to a residence permit granted under King Sigismund III Vasa of Poland (1587–1632), which forbade Jews from selling meat except in the synagogue courtyard; many were massacred during the Khmelnytsky Uprising of 1648, and the community only renewed itself in the late 18th century. By 1897, the population had grown to 1,956 (32 percent), with five synagogues and a Jewish secondary school by the early 20th century; Jews owned the town's only pharmacy, both bakeries, and all three hotels by 1914. This is the older of Novhorod-Siverskyy's two Jewish cemeteries. Novhorod-Siverskyy was the birthplace in 1904 of Zino Davidoff (born Zusele-Meer Davidov), the tobacco merchant who founded the internationally known Davidoff cigar brand. Between November 7–8, 1941, 174 Jews were shot by an SS infantry unit, and the last local Jews were killed alongside more than 17,000 Soviet prisoners of war between 1942 and 1943.
